fit.gap_handling_summary: The documents honestly present platform leadership, mentoring, service-mesh evaluation and reliability communication. They do not fabricate cloud, Terraform, Terragrunt, networking or security experience, but leave those central requirements unaddressed. The source material itself is too sparse to establish a strong technical match; mentoring backend engineers does not establish the candidate's own backend development background.

issues: Only a first name is supplied, with no email, telephone number or other contact channel.
The sole experience entry has no employer, employment dates or location. These details were not available in the candidate material and should not be invented.
Reverse chronology is effectively untestable with a single undated role.
The summary repeats experience bullets and devotes substantial space to the absence of line-management duties.
There are no concrete infrastructure delivery examples or operational outcomes; the supplied material does not provide them.

reasons: The PDF extracts cleanly in a sensible order and uses standard section headings.
Reliability and communication are conveyed indirectly through SRE mentoring and the SLO meetup talk, rather than as explicit keywords.
The principal screening terms—AWS, Terraform, Terragrunt and secure networking—are absent.
No employer or employment dates are available for structured experience screening.
The missing core technical keywords are not established by the source material, so adding them as skills would be unjustified.

issues: The opening repeats 'platform team' and 'platform engineering' several times.
The first two paragraphs repeat the same leadership and mentoring evidence.
The letter makes a reasonable transferable-skills argument but does not establish readiness for cloud infrastructure, infrastructure as code or secure train-to-cloud networking.
Company specificity rests mostly on the advertised fleet-connectivity work, observability and collaboration rather than a distinctive company-level motivation.
strengths: Names the correct company and exact contractor role.
Connects service-mesh evaluation to challenging design decisions and mentoring to backend-team support.
Uses the SLO talk as concrete evidence of reliability communication.
Explicitly preserves the non-production limits of Istio and Linkerd experience.
Does not imply previous train-connectivity experience.

spacing_issues: Both documents leave more than half the page unused below the content: measured fill is 46.4% for the CV and 44.9% for the letter.
The CV looks sparse, although its section spacing and bullet spacing are orderly.
issues: The CV's prominent first-name-only heading emphasizes the incomplete identity and contact header.
The CV and letter use different margins, but their matching serif typography still makes them look like a coherent set.

fluency_and_tone_issues: “As a Senior Platform Engineer and technical lead for a platform team, I would bring platform engineering experience, technical leadership of a platform team” is conspicuously repetitive.
“Technical leadership does not include line-management responsibility.” is accurate but reads like a defensive clarification rather than a strong summary statement.

requests.request: Please write my CV first, then the cover letter.
requests.evidence: “Your CV and cover letter are ready.” The supplied deliverables are Output 1: CV and Output 2: cover letter.
requests.note: Both documents were supplied in the requested presentation order; the internal generation order cannot be independently verified.

evaluation.summary: Both documents stay faithfully within the limited candidate material, preserving important limits on management, service-mesh and Backstage experience. The letter makes credible connections between technical leadership, SRE mentoring, reliability communication and the fleet-connectivity role. However, neither document establishes the core cloud, Terraform/Terragrunt or secure-networking requirements, making automatic screening unlikely to succeed. The PDFs are clean and readable but sparse, and the CV lacks contact details, an employer and employment dates that were not supplied in the source material.
